items.title: Can corrupted data columns from a compromised EL propagate to gossip subscribers and affect network-wide data availability?
items.test_procedure:
1. Map the P2P gossip topology for data column distribution (actor-gossip-subscriber interactions).
2. Trace how data columns flow from the publishing beacon node to subscribing peers.
3. Verify that gossip subscribers validate data columns via KZG before forwarding or storing.
4. Test whether invalid data columns are rejected at the P2P layer with appropriate error handling.
5. Assess the blast radius if validation is missing or insufficient at any hop.
6. Document the potential for denial-of-service through reputation damage to the publishing node.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-42, Supporting check for actor-gossip-subscriber. Invalid data columns could damage publisher reputation and delay data availability across the network.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-008: Does distributed blob publishing enforce subnet subscription checks before publishing data columns?
items.test_procedure:
1. Identify all code paths where data columns are published to the gossip network.
2. Review the subscription state management for custody and sampling subnets.
3. Verify that before any publish operation, the code checks if the target subnet is in the node's current subscription list.
4. Attempt to trigger a publish operation for a subnet the node is not subscribed to and verify it is blocked.
5. Test race conditions where subscription state changes during publish operations.
6. Verify error handling and logging when a publish to non-subscribed subnet is attempted.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-43, Trust Boundary: tb-008, Source Invariant: p2p:SG-010:INV-002

items.title: Does the beacon node correctly maintain and enforce the subscription state for custody and sampling subnets during blob publishing?
items.test_procedure:
1. Locate the beacon node's subscription management logic for custody and sampling subnets.
2. Trace how subscription state is initialized, updated, and queried during blob publishing.
3. Verify that subscription state is consistent across all components that perform publishing.
4. Test scenarios where subnet subscriptions are added or removed while publish operations are in progress.
5. Check for any state synchronization issues between the gossip subscriber and the publishing component.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-43, Node: actor-beacon-node, Source Invariant: p2p:SG-010:INV-002

items.title: Does the gossip subscriber properly communicate subscription state to prevent publishing on non-subscribed subnets?
items.test_procedure:
1. Review how the gossip subscriber tracks and exposes its current subnet subscriptions.
2. Identify the interface between the gossip subscriber and the blob publishing logic.
3. Verify that subscription state changes are propagated atomically and consistently.
4. Test edge cases where the gossip subscriber's internal state differs from what is exposed to publishing logic.
5. Check for any caching or stale state issues that could lead to publishing on unsubscribed subnets.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-43, Node: actor-gossip-subscriber, Source Invariant: p2p:SG-010:INV-002

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the anti-equivocation cache unconditionally updated when data columns are imported via P2P?
items.test_procedure:
1. Identify all code paths where data columns are imported into the beacon node (both via gossip and local block production).
2. Trace each import path to verify the anti-equivocation cache update is called unconditionally.
3. Check for conditional logic that could skip cache updates (e.g., publication success checks, error handling branches).
4. Create a test scenario where a data column import succeeds but gossip publication fails, and verify the cache is still updated.
5. Attempt to import conflicting data columns from the same proposer after a failed publication to verify equivocation detection still works.
6. Review error handling paths to ensure cache updates are not rolled back on subsequent failures.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-44, Trust Boundary: tb-008, Invariant: p2p:SG-010:INV-003

items.title: Can an equivocating proposer bypass anti-equivocation detection by exploiting conditional cache update logic in distributed blob publishing?
items.test_procedure:
1. Set up a test network with multiple beacon nodes subscribed to different data column subnets.
2. Craft two conflicting data column sets from the same proposer for the same slot.
3. Simulate a scenario where the first set is imported locally but publication to gossip fails or is delayed.
4. Publish the second (conflicting) set to a different subnet that the local node monitors.
5. Verify whether the local node detects the equivocation by checking if both sets are flagged as conflicting.
6. If equivocation is not detected, identify the code path that failed to update the anti-equivocation cache.
7. Document the race condition or conditional logic that enabled the bypass.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-44, Threat: stride-016, Assumption: asm-007

items.title: Does the beacon node correctly update anti-equivocation state for all data column import scenarios including local block production?
items.test_procedure:
1. Enumerate all code paths in the beacon node where data columns can be imported (gossip reception, local block production, sync, RPC).
2. For each path, verify the anti-equivocation cache update is invoked before any conditional checks.
3. Test the local block production path specifically: produce a block with data columns and verify cache update occurs.
4. Verify that cache updates happen atomically with data column storage to prevent TOCTOU issues.
5. Check that the cache key generation is consistent across all import paths to ensure proper equivocation detection.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-44, Node: actor-beacon-node

items.title: Is there a post-condition violation where anti-equivocation cache state diverges from actual imported data column state?
items.test_procedure:
1. Define the post-condition invariant: After any successful data column import, the anti-equivocation cache MUST contain an entry for that (proposer, slot, column_index) tuple.
2. Instrument the code to log cache state before and after each import operation.
3. Run a comprehensive test suite covering all import paths and verify the invariant holds.
4. Specifically test failure scenarios: partial imports, rollbacks, and error recovery paths.
5. Verify that the cache entry content matches the imported data (commitment hash) to prevent cache poisoning.
6. Test concurrent imports of the same data column to verify no race conditions in cache updates.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-44, Type: post-condition, Primary Element: p2p:SG-010:distributed_blob_publishing

items.title: Can data columns imported via distributed blob publishing bypass data availability checks or fork choice integration that would be applied to gossip-received columns?
items.test_procedure:
1. Identify the code paths for importing data columns via distributed blob publishing (e.g., EngineAPI or local import mechanisms).
2. Identify the code paths for receiving data columns via gossip (P2P layer).
3. Trace both paths to their integration points with data availability checks and fork choice processing.
4. Compare the validation steps, state updates, and downstream processing applied to columns from each source.
5. Attempt to import a data column via the distributed blob publishing path and verify it is counted for data availability in the same manner as gossip-received columns.
6. Test edge case: Import a column, then verify that a block depending on that column's availability is correctly accepted by fork choice.
7. Verify that no code paths allow imported columns to be treated as 'already validated' without performing the same checks as gossip columns.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-45, Invariant: p2p:SG-010:INV-004, Primary Element: p2p:SG-010:distributed_blob_publishing, Trust Boundary: tb-008. Bug bounty note: Demonstrate that a locally-imported data column is not counted for data availability, causing the node to reject a valid block.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-007/tb-008: Does distributed blob publishing abort when engine_getBlobsV2 returns incomplete blobs?
items.test_procedure:
1. Identify the distributed blob publishing code path that calls engine_getBlobsV2.
2. Review how the response from engine_getBlobsV2 is validated against block kzg_commitments.
3. Simulate a scenario where EL returns fewer blobs than expected (e.g., 3 of 6 blobs).
4. Verify that the publishing function aborts entirely without publishing any data columns.
5. Check for race conditions where partial data might be published before validation completes.
6. Confirm that no partial state is persisted when abort occurs.
7. Verify error logging captures the mismatch for debugging purposes.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-46, Trust Boundaries: tb-007, tb-008, Assumption: asm-006, Threat: stride-015

items.title: Does the Beacon Node correctly validate blob count from Execution Layer before initiating data column publication?
items.test_procedure:
1. Trace the data flow from engine_getBlobsV2 response handling in the Beacon Node.
2. Identify where blob count validation against kzg_commitments occurs.
3. Verify that the comparison is exact (count must match, not just be non-zero).
4. Test with edge cases: zero blobs returned, one blob missing, all blobs missing.
5. Confirm that validation happens before any publication logic is triggered.
6. Check that the validation logic cannot be bypassed through error handling paths.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-46, Node: actor-beacon-node, Assumption: asm-006

items.title: Is the atomicity of blob publishing guaranteed such that partial publication cannot occur during EL communication failures?
items.test_procedure:
1. Review the distributed blob publishing implementation for atomicity guarantees.
2. Identify all code paths that could lead to partial data column publication.
3. Test network timeout scenarios during engine_getBlobsV2 calls.
4. Verify rollback mechanisms exist if publication is interrupted mid-process.
5. Check for TOCTOU vulnerabilities between blob retrieval and publication.
6. Simulate concurrent requests that might interfere with atomicity.
7. Confirm that data availability guarantees are maintained under failure conditions.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-46, Element: p2p:SG-010:distributed_blob_publishing, Threat: stride-015

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-005: Is the BlobSidecarsByRange deprecated protocol fully disabled after FULU_FORK_EPOCH + MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS?
items.test_procedure:
1. Identify the code path handling BlobSidecarsByRange requests in the P2P layer.
2. Verify that an epoch check exists comparing current_epoch against FULU_FORK_EPOCH + MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS.
3. Simulate a request after the deprecation threshold and confirm the server returns empty or rejects the request.
4. Attempt to send malformed BlobSidecarsByRange requests post-deprecation to verify no legacy code paths are triggered.
5. Review error handling to ensure no resource exhaustion or information leakage occurs when deprecated requests are received.
6. Confirm that the protocol handler is completely unreachable (not just returning errors) after the deprecation epoch.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-47, Trust Boundary: tb-005, Source Invariant: p2p:SG-011:INV-001, Threat: stride-023

items.title: Does the beacon node properly reject deprecated BlobSidecarsByRange requests from external P2P clients after the transition period?
items.test_procedure:
1. Set up a test environment where current_epoch exceeds FULU_FORK_EPOCH + MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS.
2. From an external P2P client (actor-req-resp-client), send a BlobSidecarsByRange request to the beacon node.
3. Verify the beacon node (actor-beacon-node) either returns an empty response or explicitly rejects the request.
4. Monitor resource consumption on the beacon node to ensure no significant processing occurs for deprecated requests.
5. Test boundary conditions: send requests exactly at the deprecation epoch and one epoch before/after to verify correct threshold enforcement.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-47, Covered Nodes: actor-req-resp-client, actor-beacon-node, Trust Boundary: tb-005

items.title: Are legacy code paths for BlobSidecarsByRange properly isolated and unreachable after protocol deprecation?
items.test_procedure:
1. Perform static analysis to identify all code paths that handle BlobSidecarsByRange requests.
2. Verify that epoch validation occurs before any processing logic is invoked.
3. Confirm that no race conditions exist where requests received at the boundary epoch could still be processed.
4. Attempt to trigger legacy code paths through crafted requests that might bypass epoch checks (e.g., manipulated timestamps, replay attacks).
5. Verify that deprecated protocol handlers do not expose implementation bugs or vulnerabilities even if somehow reached.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-47, Primary Element: p2p:SG-011:blob_sidecars_by_range_deprecated, Assumption: asm-010

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-005: Is BlobSidecarsByRange request properly validated to enforce serve_range boundaries during the Fulu transition period?
items.test_procedure:
1. Identify the BlobSidecarsByRange request handler in the P2P layer.
2. Construct a request with start_slot before FULU_FORK_EPOCH and count extending past FULU_FORK_EPOCH.
3. Verify the response only includes blob sidecars from the valid serve_range [max(current_epoch - MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS, DENEB_FORK_EPOCH), FULU_FORK_EPOCH).
4. Send a request entirely at or after FULU_FORK_EPOCH and verify an empty list is returned.
5. Test edge cases: request starting exactly at FULU_FORK_EPOCH-1, request ending exactly at FULU_FORK_EPOCH.
6. Verify no crash or panic occurs when processing boundary-spanning requests.
7. Check that post-Fulu data is never served via the deprecated BlobSidecarsByRange protocol.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-48, Trust Boundary: tb-005, Invariant: p2p:SG-011:INV-002. PoC: request blob sidecars with range spanning FULU_FORK_EPOCH and observe crash or incorrect response.

items.title: Does the Request-Response Client correctly calculate and enforce the serve_range boundaries for deprecated BlobSidecarsByRange?
items.test_procedure:
1. Locate the serve_range calculation logic in the request-response client code.
2. Verify the formula: serve_range = [max(current_epoch - MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS, DENEB_FORK_EPOCH), FULU_FORK_EPOCH).
3. Test with various current_epoch values to ensure correct boundary calculation.
4. Verify that MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS is correctly applied.
5. Check that DENEB_FORK_EPOCH is used as the lower bound when current_epoch is close to genesis.
6. Confirm FULU_FORK_EPOCH is used as the exclusive upper bound.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-48, Node: actor-req-resp-client, Supporting check for boundary integrity.

items.title: Does the Beacon Node correctly filter blob sidecars to only serve pre-Fulu data via the deprecated BlobSidecarsByRange endpoint?
items.test_procedure:
1. Identify the beacon node's blob sidecar storage and retrieval logic.
2. Verify the filtering logic that prevents post-Fulu blob sidecars from being served.
3. Test that blob sidecars at exactly FULU_FORK_EPOCH are NOT served.
4. Test that blob sidecars at FULU_FORK_EPOCH - 1 ARE served (if within serve_range).
5. Verify that the beacon node returns an empty response (not an error) for out-of-range requests.
6. Check for any race conditions during the fork transition that could leak post-Fulu data.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-48, Node: actor-beacon-node, Supporting check for data filtering.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-005/tb-006: Are peers protected from scoring penalties when using deprecated BlobSidecarsByRange protocol during FULU fork transition?
items.test_procedure:
1. Identify the peer scoring logic for the BlobSidecarsByRange request handler in the P2P layer.
2. Locate the deprecated protocol handler for blob_sidecars_by_range and verify it exists for the transition period.
3. Simulate a legitimate peer sending a BlobSidecarsByRange request during FULU_FORK_EPOCH transition window.
4. Monitor peer score changes after the deprecated protocol request is processed.
5. Verify that peer score remains unchanged (no penalty applied) for using the deprecated protocol.
6. Test edge cases: requests at exact epoch boundary, requests slightly before and after the deprecation window.
7. Confirm that appropriate error responses are returned without scoring penalties.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-49, Trust Boundaries: tb-005, tb-006, Invariant: p2p:SG-011:INV-003. Network fragmentation risk if older nodes are penalized during transition.

items.title: Does the Request-Response Client (actor-req-resp-client) gracefully handle deprecated BlobSidecarsByRange responses without triggering peer penalties?
items.test_procedure:
1. Locate the request-response client code that handles BlobSidecarsByRange protocol responses.
2. Identify all code paths where peer scoring adjustments are made in the client.
3. Trace the handling of deprecated protocol responses (e.g., RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, unsupported protocol errors).
4. Verify that receiving a deprecation-related error does not decrement the peer's score.
5. Test with various deprecation error responses to ensure consistent non-penalty behavior.
6. Confirm graceful degradation: client should fall back to alternative data retrieval methods without penalizing the peer.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-49, Supporting Node: actor-req-resp-client. Client-side scoring decisions could fragment the network if deprecated protocol errors are treated as misbehavior.

items.title: Does the Beacon Node (actor-beacon-node) correctly distinguish between deprecated protocol usage and malicious peer behavior when adjusting scores?
items.test_procedure:
1. Locate the beacon node's peer scoring logic for P2P request handling.
2. Identify how the beacon node differentiates between deprecated protocol requests and invalid/malicious requests.
3. Verify that score penalty logic includes explicit checks for FULU_FORK_EPOCH transition period.
4. Test that deprecated BlobSidecarsByRange requests from peers are not classified as protocol violations.
5. Confirm that the scoring system has a whitelist or exception for deprecated protocols during transition.
6. Verify logging: deprecated protocol usage should be logged at INFO/DEBUG level, not WARNING/ERROR.
7. Test that legitimate deprecation does not trigger rate limiting or connection termination.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-49, Supporting Node: actor-beacon-node. Beacon node is responsible for maintaining network connectivity during protocol transitions.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the ENR eth2 field validated to be exactly 16 bytes before SSZ deserialization?
items.test_procedure:
1. Identify the ENR parsing code path that handles the eth2 field in the P2P discovery layer.
2. Locate the SSZ deserialization function for ENRForkID and verify it validates input length before parsing.
3. Craft an ENR record with an eth2 field shorter than 16 bytes (e.g., 8 bytes) and submit via P2P discovery.
4. Craft an ENR record with an eth2 field longer than 16 bytes (e.g., 32 bytes) and submit via P2P discovery.
5. Verify both malformed ENR records are rejected with appropriate error handling (no crash, no buffer over-read).
6. Check that error messages do not leak internal memory contents or sensitive information.
7. Verify the peer is not added to the peer table when ENR validation fails.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-50, Trust Boundary: tb-009, Invariant: p2p:SG-012:INV-001

items.title: Can a malicious P2P peer cause buffer over-read or under-read by sending ENR eth2 fields with invalid lengths?
items.test_procedure:
1. Review the SSZ deserialization code for ENRForkID to identify how it handles length validation.
2. Trace the data flow from raw P2P message receipt to ENRForkID struct population.
3. Test with eth2 field containing 0 bytes (empty) to verify rejection without crash.
4. Test with eth2 field containing 15 bytes (one byte short) to verify rejection.
5. Test with eth2 field containing 17 bytes (one byte extra) to verify rejection.
6. Use memory sanitizers (ASan/MSan) during testing to detect any buffer over-read or under-read.
7. Verify that rejected ENR records do not cause the node to disconnect from the P2P network.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-50, Trust Boundary: tb-009, Threat: stride-017

items.title: Does the beacon node properly reject peers with invalid ENR eth2 fields during discovery handshake?
items.test_procedure:
1. Identify the peer discovery handshake flow between actor-p2p-peer and actor-beacon-node.
2. Locate where ENR records are exchanged and validated during peer discovery.
3. Set up a test P2P peer that advertises an ENR with a malformed eth2 field.
4. Attempt to connect to the beacon node and observe if the connection is rejected.
5. Verify that the beacon node logs an appropriate warning/error for the invalid ENR.
6. Confirm the malicious peer is not added to the peer routing table.
7. Test that repeated invalid ENR attempts trigger rate limiting or peer banning.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-50, Covered nodes: actor-p2p-peer, actor-beacon-node

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-009: Does BPO fork ENR eth2 field computation correctly preserve next_fork_version equal to current_fork_version?
items.test_procedure:
1. Identify the ENR eth2 field computation code path for BPO (Blob Parameter Only) forks.
2. Verify that for BPO forks, next_fork_version is set equal to current_fork_version (not a new version).
3. Confirm that next_fork_epoch is set to the planned BPO fork epoch.
4. Compare the implementation against regular fork handling where next_fork_version != current_fork_version.
5. Test peer discovery between two nodes at a BPO fork boundary to ensure they correctly discover each other.
6. Attempt to trigger network fragmentation by manipulating ENR eth2 field values at BPO fork boundaries.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-51, Trust Boundary: tb-009, Source Invariant: p2p:SG-012:INV-002, Source Threat: stride-018

items.title: Does the P2P peer actor correctly validate incoming ENR eth2 fields for BPO fork compatibility?
items.test_procedure:
1. Locate the ENR validation logic in the P2P peer handling code.
2. Verify that BPO fork detection correctly identifies when a fork is BPO vs. regular.
3. Test that peers with correctly computed BPO fork ENR eth2 fields are accepted.
4. Test that peers with incorrectly computed ENR eth2 fields (next_fork_version != current_fork_version for BPO) are handled appropriately.
5. Verify the validation logic does not inadvertently reject compatible peers at BPO fork boundaries.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-51, Supporting Node: actor-p2p-peer, Source Invariant: p2p:SG-012:INV-002

items.title: Does the beacon node correctly compute and advertise ENR eth2 field for BPO forks?
items.test_procedure:
1. Locate the beacon node's ENR eth2 field computation logic.
2. Identify how the beacon node determines whether an upcoming fork is BPO or regular.
3. Verify the beacon node sets next_fork_version = current_fork_version for BPO forks.
4. Verify the beacon node sets next_fork_epoch to the planned BPO epoch.
5. Test beacon node ENR advertisement at various epochs relative to a BPO fork activation.
6. Compare ENR output between different client implementations to ensure consistency.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-51, Supporting Node: actor-beacon-node, Source Invariant: p2p:SG-012:INV-002

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-009: Is the ENR eth2 field correctly signaling no upcoming fork by setting next_fork_version == current_fork_version AND next_fork_epoch == FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH?
items.test_procedure:
1. Identify the ENR eth2 field computation logic in the beacon node codebase (p2p:SG-012:enr_eth2_field_computation).
2. Review the code path that determines when no fork is planned and how the ENR fields are set.
3. Verify that when no fork is scheduled, next_fork_version is set equal to current_fork_version.
4. Verify that when no fork is scheduled, next_fork_epoch is set to FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH (0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF or equivalent).
5. Test by simulating a state with no planned fork and inspecting the advertised ENR eth2 field values.
6. Verify that peers correctly interpret the no-fork signal and do not reject the node as being on a different fork schedule.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-52, Trust Boundary: tb-009, Invariant: p2p:SG-012:INV-003, Threat: stride-017

items.title: Does the beacon node (actor-beacon-node) correctly compute ENR eth2 fields for peer discovery when transitioning between fork states?
items.test_procedure:
1. Locate the beacon node's ENR update logic that handles fork schedule changes.
2. Review state transitions: verify the node correctly updates ENR fields when moving from 'fork planned' to 'no fork planned' state.
3. Test edge case: immediately after a fork completes, verify the node resets next_fork_version and next_fork_epoch to the no-fork values.
4. Verify that ENR updates are propagated to peers in a timely manner after fork state changes.
5. Check for race conditions where ENR might temporarily advertise stale fork information.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-52, Supporting Node: actor-beacon-node, Invariant: p2p:SG-012:INV-003

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-009: Does the ENR eth2 field computation use wall-clock time instead of sync state for epoch determination?
items.test_procedure:
1. Identify the code responsible for computing the ENR eth2 field fork_digest in the beacon node.
2. Trace the epoch value used in fork_digest calculation to determine its source (wall-clock vs sync state).
3. Set up a test node that is still syncing (behind chain head by multiple epochs).
4. Capture the ENR advertisement from the syncing node and extract the fork_digest field.
5. Compare the advertised fork_digest against what would be expected from: (a) wall-clock epoch, (b) sync-state epoch.
6. Verify that the fork_digest matches the wall-clock epoch, not the synced-to epoch.
7. Test across a simulated fork boundary where a syncing node would be behind the fork but wall-clock time is past the fork.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-53, Trust Boundary: tb-009, Invariant: p2p:SG-012:INV-004. A syncing node using sync-state epoch would advertise a pre-fork fork_digest after the fork has occurred, causing it to be filtered out by fully-synced peers.

items.title: Can a syncing beacon node become isolated from the P2P network by advertising an incorrect pre-fork fork_digest?
items.test_procedure:
1. Deploy a test beacon node and allow it to fully sync to chain head.
2. Configure a second test node to start syncing from genesis (or significantly behind chain head).
3. Simulate a network fork transition while the second node is still syncing.
4. Monitor peer discovery attempts from the syncing node to fully-synced peers.
5. Verify whether the syncing node can successfully connect to post-fork peers.
6. Check ENR advertisements from the syncing node for fork_digest correctness.
7. Document any peer filtering or connection rejections that occur due to fork_digest mismatch.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-53, Node: actor-beacon-node. Bug bounty target: Demonstrate a syncing node being isolated because it advertises pre-fork fork_digest.

items.title: Does the beacon node correctly update its ENR eth2 field when wall-clock time crosses a fork epoch boundary?
items.test_procedure:
1. Identify the ENR update mechanism and the trigger for eth2 field updates.
2. Set up a beacon node with a known fork schedule where a fork is imminent.
3. Monitor the node's ENR eth2 field continuously as wall-clock time approaches the fork epoch.
4. Verify that the ENR is updated precisely when wall-clock time crosses the fork boundary.
5. Confirm that the update occurs regardless of the node's sync state (even if still syncing pre-fork blocks).
6. Test edge cases: node restart near fork boundary, network partition during fork transition.
7. Validate that the sequence number in ENR is incremented appropriately on fork_digest change.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W4B13-53, Trust Boundary: tb-009. Fork transitions must be handled based on wall-clock time to prevent bootstrapping problems.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Can the slotted_freezable mechanism for Header objects be bypassed?
items.test_procedure: 1. Attempt to modify Header fields after freeze() is called. 2. Test __dict__ manipulation on frozen Header objects. 3. Try subclassing Header to bypass freeze mechanism. 4. Verify that all modification attempts raise appropriate errors.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-17, Trust Boundary: tb-005. Internal-only reachability but high impact if bypassed.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are all 21 header fields validated before block acceptance?
items.test_procedure: 1. Craft blocks with zero/default values for computed fields (base_fee_per_gas, requests_hash, blob_gas_used). 2. Submit via P2P and verify rejection. 3. Test each of the 21 header fields individually with missing/default values. 4. Verify block validation detects and rejects incomplete headers.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-18, Trust Boundary: tb-005. Bug bounty eligible - PoC requires block with zero-valued computed field being accepted.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is base_fee_per_gas independently recomputed per EIP-1559?
items.test_procedure: 1. Construct block with incorrect base_fee_per_gas (not matching EIP-1559 formula). 2. Submit via P2P. 3. Verify block is rejected. 4. Test boundary cases where parent gas_used is at limits. 5. Verify the adjustment formula is applied correctly.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-19, Trust Boundary: tb-005. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is blob gas accounting validated per EIP-4844 under Fusaka rules?
items.test_procedure: 1. Construct block with incorrect blob_gas_used or excess_blob_gas. 2. Test with Fusaka-specific blob gas parameters. 3. Verify rejection of blocks with invalid blob gas values. 4. Test edge cases at the new Fusaka blob gas limits.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-20, Trust Boundary: tb-005. Fusaka-specific - higher risk of implementation inconsistencies.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is requests_hash validated per EIP-7685 under Fusaka?
items.test_procedure: 1. Construct block with incorrect requests_hash. 2. Submit via P2P under Fusaka rules. 3. Verify block rejection. 4. Test EIP-7685 computation rules are correctly implemented. 5. Verify requests_hash is independently computed, not trusted from header.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-21, Trust Boundary: tb-005. Fusaka-specific EIP - high priority.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are non-empty ommers rejected in post-merge blocks?
items.test_procedure: 1. Construct post-merge Osaka block with non-empty ommers list. 2. Submit via P2P. 3. Verify body-level validation rejects the block. 4. Confirm both header (ommers_hash) and body (ommers tuple) validation occurs.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-23, Trust Boundary: tb-001. Data smuggling risk via ommer fields.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are all 5 transaction types decoded without type confusion?
items.test_procedure: 1. Construct blocks with each transaction type (Legacy, AccessList, FeeMarket, Blob, SetCode). 2. Test mixed blocks with all types. 3. Verify no type confusion between Bytes and LegacyTransaction representations. 4. Test edge cases in transaction type detection.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-24, Trust Boundary: tb-001. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is Withdrawal object immutability enforced after freeze()?
items.test_procedure: 1. Create Withdrawal object and call freeze(). 2. Attempt to modify index, validator_index, address, and amount fields. 3. Verify all modification attempts raise errors. 4. Test __dict__ manipulation bypass attempts.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-25, Trust Boundary: tb-004. Internal reachability via Engine API.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are incomplete Withdrawal objects rejected during construction?
items.test_procedure: 1. Attempt to construct Withdrawal with missing fields. 2. Test each field individually (index, validator_index, address, amount). 3. Verify construction errors are raised for incomplete objects. 4. Test default value handling.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-26, Trust Boundary: tb-004.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are withdrawal addresses and amounts type-validated?
items.test_procedure: 1. Verify withdrawal address must be valid 20-byte Address. 2. Verify amount must be valid U256. 3. Test with invalid address lengths. 4. Test with amounts exceeding U256 bounds. 5. Confirm EL trusts but type-validates CL data.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-27, Trust Boundary: tb-004. CL trust assumption - EL does not verify withdrawal amounts.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is ETH credited only to addresses specified by CL?
items.test_procedure: 1. Trace withdrawal processing code path. 2. Verify ETH is credited exactly to the address in each Withdrawal object. 3. Check for any address modification or substitution during processing. 4. Audit the withdrawal crediting function.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-28, Trust Boundary: tb-004. Requires CL compromise to exploit.

items.title: Is the bloom filter bytearray always exactly 256 bytes with no out-of-bounds access?
items.test_procedure: 1. Review add_to_bloom function for bounds checking. 2. Craft transactions producing logs with adversarial addresses/topics. 3. Verify bloom bytearray is always 256 bytes. 4. Test for index values that could exceed [0, 255].
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-29. Bug bounty eligible - PoC must demonstrate out-of-bounds access.

items.title: Is the 11-bit mask (0x07FF) correctly applied in bloom bit computation?
items.test_procedure: 1. Verify bit_to_set = Uint.from_be_bytes(hash[idx:idx+2]) AND 0x07FF. 2. Check for incorrect mask values (e.g., 0x0FFF). 3. Verify bit_to_set is always in [0, 2047]. 4. Test with hash values that would exceed bounds without proper masking.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-30. Incorrect mask causes consensus splits.

items.title: Is byte_index computation always in range [0, 255]?
items.test_procedure: 1. Verify formula: bit_index = 0x07FF - bit_to_set, byte_index = bit_index // 8. 2. Test boundary cases where bit_to_set = 0 and bit_to_set = 2047. 3. Confirm byte_index always in [0, 255] given correct mask.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-31. Derived invariant from mask correctness.

items.title: Does add_to_bloom iterate exactly 3 times reading 2-byte pairs?
items.test_procedure: 1. Review add_to_bloom loop structure. 2. Verify exactly 3 iterations reading indices (0, 2, 4). 3. Verify each iteration sets exactly one bit. 4. Check for off-by-one in loop bounds.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-32. Incorrect iteration count causes bloom divergence.

items.title: Is bloom filter initialized to 256 zero bytes before processing logs?
items.test_procedure: 1. Review logs_bloom initialization code. 2. Check for buffer reuse without clearing. 3. Verify bloom is fresh 256 zero bytes before each computation. 4. Test for residual bits from previous computations.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-34. Memory optimization bugs could cause contamination.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is every log address added to bloom exactly once?
items.test_procedure: 1. Trace bloom computation for receipts with multiple logs. 2. Verify each log address is processed exactly once. 3. Check for skipped addresses in edge cases. 4. Test with many logs in a single receipt.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-35, Trust Boundary: tb-008. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is every log topic added to bloom exactly once?
items.test_procedure: 1. Verify add_to_bloom calls = (1 + len(log.topics)) per log. 2. Test logs with 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 topics. 3. Check for skipped topics. 4. Verify total bloom bit count matches expected.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-36, Trust Boundary: tb-008. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Is Bloom returned only after all logs are fully processed?
items.test_procedure: 1. Review logs_bloom for early return paths. 2. Check for race conditions in log processing. 3. Verify bloom construction completes before return. 4. Test exception handling during log processing.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-37. Early return produces partial bloom.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is receipt bloom consistency with logs verified?
items.test_procedure: 1. Construct receipt with bloom inconsistent with logs. 2. Submit block via P2P. 3. Verify bloom is recomputed and compared. 4. Confirm blocks with inconsistent blooms are rejected.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-38, Trust Boundary: tb-008. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is cumulative_gas_used monotonically non-decreasing?
items.test_procedure: 1. Construct block with receipts where cumulative_gas_used decreases. 2. Submit via P2P. 3. Verify block rejection. 4. Test consecutive receipt pairs for monotonicity validation.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-40, Trust Boundary: tb-001, tb-003. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are logs with more than 4 topics rejected?
items.test_procedure: 1. Review EVM LOG0-LOG4 opcode handlers. 2. Verify no opcode allows more than 4 topics. 3. Test for bugs in opcode handling that could produce excess topics. 4. Verify topic count validation during transaction execution.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-42, Trust Boundary: tb-003. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are oversized blocks rejected per EIP-7934?
items.test_procedure: 1. Construct block exceeding EIP-7934 RLP size limit. 2. Verify early rejection before full deserialization. 3. Test boundary at exact size limit. 4. Measure resource consumption for oversized blocks.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-43, Trust Boundary: tb-001. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is bloom bit arithmetic spec-compliant across implementations?
items.test_procedure: 1. Verify exact formula: bit_to_set = Uint.from_be_bytes(hash[idx:idx+2]) AND 0x07FF. 2. Verify bit_index = 0x07FF - bit_to_set. 3. Verify byte_index = bit_index // 8. 4. Verify bit_value = 1 << (7 - (bit_index % 8)). 5. Cross-check against other client implementations.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-44, Trust Boundary: tb-008. CRITICAL - any deviation causes consensus split.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is bloom computation bounded by gas limits?
items.test_procedure: 1. Craft transactions maximizing log output within gas limit. 2. Measure bloom computation time. 3. Verify O(n) complexity in total log entries. 4. Confirm gas limits bound computation.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-45, Trust Boundary: tb-008. Conditional scope - known design limitation.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is bloom keccak256 call count bounded?
items.test_procedure: 1. Count keccak256 calls during max-log block processing. 2. Verify bound: (1 + max_topics_per_log) * max_logs_per_block. 3. Test at EIP-7825 and EIP-7934 limits.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-46, Trust Boundary: tb-008. Conditional scope - bounded by gas.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is gas_used <= gas_limit enforced?
items.test_procedure: 1. Construct block with gas_used > gas_limit. 2. Submit via P2P. 3. Verify block rejection. 4. Test at exact boundary (gas_used == gas_limit).
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-49, Trust Boundary: tb-001. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is header bloom verified against computed receipt blooms?
items.test_procedure: 1. Construct block with header bloom != combined receipt blooms. 2. Submit via P2P. 3. Verify block rejection. 4. Test bloom combination logic across receipts.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-50, Trust Boundary: tb-001, tb-008. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is parent_hash validated against canonical chain?
items.test_procedure: 1. Construct block with fabricated parent_hash. 2. Submit via P2P. 3. Verify block is rejected or deferred. 4. Test with parent_hash of orphaned/non-canonical blocks.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-51, Trust Boundary: tb-001. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is timestamp > parent.timestamp enforced?
items.test_procedure: 1. Construct block with timestamp <= parent.timestamp. 2. Submit via P2P. 3. Verify block rejection. 4. Test timestamp == parent.timestamp edge case.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-52, Trust Boundary: tb-001. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is extra_data limited to 32 bytes?
items.test_procedure: 1. Construct block with extra_data > 32 bytes. 2. Submit via P2P. 3. Verify block rejection. 4. Test at exactly 32 bytes and 33 bytes.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-53, Trust Boundary: tb-001. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is block number == parent.number + 1 validated?
items.test_procedure: 1. Construct block with incorrect block number. 2. Test number = parent.number (same). 3. Test number = parent.number + 2 (skip). 4. Verify all variants rejected.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-54, Trust Boundary: tb-001. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is state_root verified after full block execution?
items.test_procedure: 1. Construct valid-looking block with incorrect state_root. 2. Execute all transactions. 3. Verify state_root recomputation. 4. Confirm mismatch causes rejection.
items.notes: Source: PROP-W7B16-55, Trust Boundary: tb-001. CRITICAL - state_root bypass breaks consensus.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is trie root computation deterministic regardless of insertion order?
items.test_procedure: 1. Create identical trie states with different insertion orders. 2. Compute root() for each. 3. Verify all roots are identical. 4. Test with large key sets and varied orderings.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0001, Trust Boundary: tb-006. CRITICAL - non-determinism causes network-wide consensus failure.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does patricialize terminate for all valid inputs?
items.test_procedure: 1. Verify level parameter strictly increases on each recursive call. 2. Test with keys at maximum nibble length (64 for secured tries). 3. Check for infinite recursion conditions. 4. Test all trie modes (secured and unsecured).
items.notes: Source: PROP-0002, Trust Boundary: tb-001, tb-008. CRITICAL - infinite recursion halts network.

items.title: Are default values excluded from trie._data (no ghost entries)?
items.test_procedure: 1. Set key to non-default value, then set to default. 2. Verify key is removed from _data. 3. Check trie._data.keys() after deletion. 4. Verify no ghost entries in Merkle root computation.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0003. CRITICAL - ghost entries corrupt state root.

items.title: Does trie_get return the exact value set by trie_set?
items.test_procedure: 1. Set various key-value pairs. 2. Get each key and verify exact value match. 3. Test with edge case values (empty, large, special characters). 4. Test unset keys return trie.default.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0004. CRITICAL - incorrect reads break EVM execution.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are secured trie keys always keccak256 hashed?
items.test_procedure: 1. Verify _prepare_trie hashes keys when trie.secured=True. 2. Check for code paths bypassing key hashing. 3. Verify no raw keys appear in secured trie mapping. 4. Test for trie-balancing attack vectors.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0005, Trust Boundary: tb-007. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Does encode_node always produce non-empty output?
items.test_procedure: 1. Test encode_node with all value types. 2. Verify assertion for v != b''. 3. Look for edge cases producing empty bytes. 4. Test with unusual Account, Transaction, Receipt values.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0006. Empty encoding crashes or corrupts trie.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is get_storage_root always invoked for Account encoding?
items.test_procedure: 1. Trace Account encoding path. 2. Verify get_storage_root is called. 3. Test with newly created accounts. 4. Verify None return causes failure (not silent success).
items.notes: Source: PROP-0007, Trust Boundary: tb-002. CRITICAL - missing storage root corrupts state.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does get_storage_root return correct canonical roots?
items.test_procedure: 1. Verify storage root computation for various accounts. 2. Test accounts with empty storage (should return EMPTY_TRIE_ROOT). 3. Compare computed roots against known correct values. 4. Test edge cases triggering callback.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0008, Trust Boundary: tb-002. CRITICAL - incorrect storage root silently corrupts state.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the 32-byte threshold in encode_internal_node exact?
items.test_procedure: 1. Test with RLP encoding exactly 31, 32, 33 bytes. 2. Verify < 32 returns unencoded, >= 32 returns hash. 3. Check for off-by-one errors. 4. Cross-reference against Ethereum specification.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0010, Trust Boundary: tb-004, tb-005. CRITICAL - boundary error causes consensus split.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is RLP encoding deterministic and canonical?
items.test_procedure: 1. Encode same input multiple times. 2. Verify bit-identical output. 3. Test with complex nested structures. 4. Compare against canonical RLP specification.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0011, Trust Boundary: tb-004. CRITICAL - non-canonical RLP breaks consensus.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is keccak256 deterministic and collision-resistant?
items.test_procedure: 1. Hash same input multiple times. 2. Verify identical 32-byte output. 3. Verify against known keccak256 test vectors. 4. Check for library version/configuration issues.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0012, Trust Boundary: tb-005. CRITICAL - any inconsistency breaks all trie operations.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is keccak256 collision resistance maintained?
items.test_procedure: 1. Verify 128-bit collision resistance is intact. 2. Monitor for cryptanalytic advances. 3. Test address collision scenarios (theoretical). 4. Confirm collision would allow state overwrites.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0013, Trust Boundary: tb-005, tb-007. CRITICAL - collision enables fund theft.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is encode_node type dispatch correct?
items.test_procedure: 1. Test each type: Account, LegacyTransaction, Receipt, Withdrawal, U256, Bytes. 2. Verify correct dispatch path for each. 3. Test fallback to previous_trie.encode_node. 4. Check isinstance chain ordering.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0014, Trust Boundary: tb-003. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is previous_trie fallback encoding compatible?
items.test_procedure: 1. Identify types that fall through to previous_trie. 2. Verify encoding produces non-empty bytes. 3. Check RLP-encodability of output. 4. Test cross-fork encoding consistency.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0015, Trust Boundary: tb-003. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Does copy_trie produce a fully independent copy?
items.test_procedure: 1. Copy trie and modify the copy. 2. Verify original is unchanged. 3. Test with various value types. 4. Verify state snapshot/revert behavior.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0016. Failed transaction reverts would not work correctly.

items.title: Does trie_set correctly delete keys when value equals default?
items.test_procedure: 1. Set key to value, then set to trie.default. 2. Verify key is absent from _data. 3. Test with storage slot zero (common deletion case). 4. Verify no ghost entry persists.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0018. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Is trie_set a no-op when deleting non-existent key?
items.test_procedure: 1. Set non-existent key to trie.default. 2. Verify _data is unchanged. 3. Check root() before and after (should be identical). 4. Test with various key formats.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0019. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Does trie_get return trie.default for unset keys?
items.test_procedure: 1. Get key that was never set. 2. Verify return value is exactly trie.default. 3. Test identity comparison (not just equality). 4. Test various key formats.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0020. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Are nibble values validated to be in range [0, 15]?
items.test_procedure: 1. Check bytes_to_nibble_list output range. 2. Look for code paths bypassing nibble conversion. 3. Test nibble_list_to_compact with out-of-range values. 4. Verify bit masking guarantees.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0023. Conditional scope - normally guaranteed by bytes_to_nibble_list.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is compact encoding header byte correct?
items.test_procedure: 1. Test even-length leaf (expect 0x20). 2. Test even-length extension (expect 0x00). 3. Test odd-length leaf (expect 0x3X). 4. Test odd-length extension (expect 0x1X). 5. Verify Merkle proof compatibility.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0024, Trust Boundary: tb-006. CRITICAL - incorrect header breaks proofs.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does empty trie produce EMPTY_TRIE_ROOT?
items.test_procedure: 1. Create empty trie and compute root(). 2. Verify result equals keccak256(rlp.encode(b'')). 3. Test after deleting all entries from non-empty trie. 4. Verify newly created accounts have correct empty storage root.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0028, Trust Boundary: tb-006. CRITICAL - affects all accounts.

items.title: Does single-element trie produce correct LeafNode?
items.test_procedure: 1. Create trie with single key-value. 2. Verify patricialize returns LeafNode. 3. Check key suffix matches key[level:]. 4. Test contracts with single storage slot.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0029. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Are ExtensionNodes correctly constructed for shared prefixes?
items.test_procedure: 1. Create keys with common prefix. 2. Verify ExtensionNode key_segment equals shared prefix. 3. Verify subnode is recursive patricialize result. 4. Check level increment equals prefix length.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0030. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Are BranchNodes correctly constructed with 16 subnodes?
items.test_procedure: 1. Create keys with no shared prefix at current level. 2. Verify BranchNode has exactly 16 subnodes. 3. Verify each subnode contains only keys with matching nibble. 4. Test key distribution correctness.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0031. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Is Account/Receipt/Uint rejected at BranchNode value position?
items.test_procedure: 1. Identify conditions where len(key) == level. 2. Test with Account/Receipt/Uint at this position. 3. Verify AssertionError is raised. 4. Test edge cases in secured tries.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0032. Conditional scope - unusual state configuration required.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does root() always return exactly 32 bytes?
items.test_procedure: 1. Compute root() for various trie states. 2. Verify all results are exactly 32 bytes. 3. Test small tries where RLP < 32 bytes. 4. Verify correct hashing for small root nodes.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0033, Trust Boundary: tb-006. CRITICAL - non-32-byte root breaks headers.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are pathological trie structures prevented?
items.test_procedure: 1. Test unsecured tries with crafted keys. 2. Measure depth/balance of resulting structures. 3. Benchmark root computation time. 4. Verify secured tries mitigate via key hashing.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0034, Trust Boundary: tb-001, tb-007. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are new types explicitly handled, not falling through?
items.test_procedure: 1. Review isinstance chain for all expected types. 2. Verify no unintended fallthrough to previous_trie. 3. Test fork upgrade scenarios. 4. Check for new types added in Fusaka.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0035, Trust Boundary: tb-003. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is state growth bounded by gas costs?
items.test_procedure: 1. Craft transactions maximizing state entries per gas. 2. Measure actual state growth vs gas spent. 3. Verify SSTORE/CREATE gas costs match spec. 4. Test root computation time bounds.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0038, Trust Boundary: tb-001, tb-006. Bug bounty eligible.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are small root nodes hashed to 32 bytes?
items.test_procedure: 1. Create trie with minimal entries. 2. Verify root_node with RLP < 32 bytes is hashed. 3. Verify final root is 32 bytes. 4. Test various small trie configurations.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0040, Trust Boundary: tb-006. CRITICAL - short root breaks headers.

items.title: Does _prepare_trie process ALL entries in trie._data?
items.test_procedure: 1. Count entries before and after _prepare_trie. 2. Verify no entries are skipped. 3. Check exception handling for potential silent failures. 4. Test with various value types.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0041. CRITICAL - skipped entries cause state loss.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are secured trie key collisions prevented?
items.test_procedure: 1. Verify keccak256 collision resistance. 2. Test _prepare_trie output for key uniqueness. 3. Verify second entry would overwrite first on collision. 4. Confirm collision is computationally infeasible.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0042, Trust Boundary: tb-005, tb-007. CRITICAL - collision enables theft.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is root computation order-independent?
items.test_procedure: 1. Test with different dict iteration orders (if possible). 2. Verify patricialize produces canonical structure regardless of order. 3. Compare roots from different orderings. 4. Test across Python versions.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0044, Trust Boundary: tb-006. CRITICAL - order-dependence causes splits.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are Accounts correctly routed through encode_node?
items.test_procedure: 1. Trace Account encoding path in _prepare_trie. 2. Verify isinstance(value, Account) check. 3. Test with Account-like but non-Account objects. 4. Verify storage root is included for Accounts only.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0046, Trust Boundary: tb-002. CRITICAL - misclassification corrupts state.

items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is root() cross-implementation compatible?
items.test_procedure: 1. Compare root() output against other Ethereum clients. 2. Test with known state configurations. 3. Run consensus test vectors. 4. Verify against official test suites.
items.notes: Source: PROP-0047, Trust Boundary: tb-006. CRITICAL - divergence breaks network.
